item.title: UK PM weighs delay to roadmap for higher defence spending, Times reports
item.description:
LONDON, Oct 6 (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering delaying an announcement on how and when Britain will raise defence spending to 3% of GDP, The Times reported on Tuesday, pushing back a key milestone on the path to meeting NATO's target of 3.5% by 2035.

Britain is under pressure to spell out how it will meet the NATO commitment and respond to a heightened security threat.

Burnham has pledged to meet the 2035 target, but his government has yet to set out the steps required to get there.

item.title: Explainer-One year on, Trump's Gaza plan has not stopped Israeli fire or disarmed Hamas
item.description:
JERUSALEM, Oct 6 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump’s year-old plan to end the Gaza war has stalled, with Israel mounting near daily attacks and occupying around two-thirds of the shattered enclave where Palestinians face dire conditions.

The initial phase resulted in a ceasefire on October 10, 2025 and secured the release of the last remaining hostages seized in Hamas’ 2023 attacks on Israel, along with freedom for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners and detainees held by Israel.

item.title: Britain likely to expel Israeli diplomats if Jerusalem consulate closes, sources say
item.description:
(Corrects number of sources in paragraph 10, changing reference to 'fifth source' from 'fourth source')

By Alexander Cornwell

TEL AVIV, Oct 6 (Reuters) - Britain is likely to expel Israeli diplomats if Israel carries out its order to shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem this week in a dispute over sanctions targeting Israeli settlements, four sources said.

item.title: Explainer-How is the Nobel Peace Prize decided?
item.description:
By Gwladys Fouche

OSLO, Oct 6 (Reuters) - The Nobel Peace Prize will be announced on Friday. Here is a look at how the award works:

WHO IS NOMINATED?

Some 287 candidates have been nominated,including 208 individuals and 79 organisations. We don't know who because the list is kept secret for 50 years, inside a vault in the basement of the Norwegian Nobel Institute in Oslo.

Still, nominators, of whom there are thousands worldwide, can choose to reveal their choices.

IS US PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP NOMINATED AND CAN HE WIN?

item.title: Flydubai co-pilot completed portion of his flight training in New Zealand, police says
item.description:
By Lucy Craymer

WELLINGTON, Oct 6 (Reuters) - The flydubai co-pilot who stabbed his captain in an alleged attempt to crash a plane last week was in New Zealand seven years ago to complete a portion of his flight training for a U.K.-based company, New Zealand police said in a statement on Tuesday.

Police said the man was in New Zealand between November 2018 and May 2019 on a six-month student visa.

item.title: War-weary northern Israelis rethink loyalty to Netanyahu before election
item.description:
On Israel's border with Lebanon where Hezbollah fired thousands of rockets and drones, previous backers of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu say they are rethinking how they will vote in the first election since the war.

"Many I know were right-wing and were Bibi supporters, and today they're not," said plant nursery owner Sigal Malachi, using a nickname for Israel's longest-serving premier.

item.title: US envoy attends event with Sudanese army chief in Egypt
item.description:
By Kanishka Singh

WASHINGTON, Oct 5 (Reuters) - An envoy of President Donald Trump said he attended an event over the weekend with the head of Sudan's army, which is fighting a war with paramilitary forces that has created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

DETAILS:

• US Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos said on X he attended a lunch hosted by Egypt's President Abdel Fattah ​al-Sisi alongside Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
